partner_applied.application: For Q_m=2X1<c1,Y>+2X2<c2,Y>+<v,Y>^2 with three disjoint size-m flat physical banks, G=I_3, lambda=1 and rho=(1-1/m)^3. The partner r=1 theorem gives ||p_Q||inf<3.157 at m=16. Its quotient form gives ||p_Q||inf <=(5/3)e^(3/5)[rho |lambda| det(C^T P_(v^perp) C)]^(-1/5).

new_claims.statement: For W=[V,C], det(W^TW)=det(V^TV)det(C^T P_(V^perp)C). Physical hub directions are counted modulo the displayed curvature span.
For r>2 exact displayed leaf-square directions with Pluecker disjointness rho>0, ||p_Q||inf <= [r/(r-2)]e[rho det(V^TV)prod|lambda|]^(-1/r), with a continuous density.
If theta is deleted full-frame leverage and q is the maximum surviving full-frame leverage in a d-dimensional coefficient frame, theta+dq<1 implies rho_I det(G_I)>=(1-theta-dq)det G.
For h literal hubs and a surviving diagonal-plus-rank-r leaf packet, r+2h>2 and theta+(r+h)q<1 imply a continuous density with ||p_Q||inf<=C_(h,r)[(1-theta-(r+h)q)det(G)prod|lambda|]^(-1/(r+2h)).

next_step: Show that failure of every quantitative quotient-frame puncture certificate forces an already-paid bounded physical core, physical pair, ridge/diffuse, grouped-square or cross-volume/tail branch. The survivor must concentrate nontrivial coefficient leverage on rows that cannot be conditioned away.
